key_concepts: A compound light microscope is used to observe cells and small specimens
The ocular lens or eyepiece is the part you look through
The body tube holds the lenses and connects the eyepiece to the objectives
The revolving nosepiece holds and rotates the objective lenses
Low-power and high-power objective lenses differ in length and magnification
Coarse and fine adjustment knobs are used to focus the specimen
Magnification power is calculated by multiplying eyepiece and objective lens magnification
A specimen is the sample placed on a glass slide for observation
The mirror or illuminator supplies light to make the specimen visible
Carry a microscope with two hands to prevent dropping
Remove the slide and cover the microscope with a dust cover when storing
To observe a specimen, place the slide on the stage, secure it with stage clips, and adjus
